title: Claude Code runtime guard for canonical task ownership
objective: Enforce the existing provider-neutral claim-before-edit contract in Claude Code by blocking Write, Edit, and Bash calls until Claude owns exactly one active task, while keeping .ai task records authoritative and the hook a replaceable vendor adapter.
validations: node --test tools/scripts/agent-task-guard.test.mjs passes 11/11 deterministic guard cases.
Direct PreToolUse CLI simulation returns exit 2 for an unclaimed mutation and exit 0 for read-only inspection and task-record bootstrap.
Shared and local Claude settings parse; the project matcher is Write|Edit|Bash, the command references the canonical guard, and local settings do not disable hooks.
Task, handoff, and settings JSON parse; local Markdown links in all affected documentation resolve.
The coordination validator passes with 16 task records after the immutable Claude handoff was added.
git diff --check passes with only the repository's existing LF-to-CRLF checkout warnings.
No dependency, lockfile, Graph IR extractor, generated graph, Nx project, CI workflow, master source, or current planning file was changed.
risks: Bash requires a unique active claim, but arbitrary shell text cannot be proven to touch only declared paths before execution; completion diff review remains mandatory.
Project-level hooks can be disabled by higher-precedence local settings and are not equivalent to enterprise managed policy; the owner must verify the Project hook through /hooks.
The claude executable is unavailable in the current PowerShell PATH, so the active IDE client's version and hook UI could not be verified from this shell.
Codex, Gemini, and non-Claude-Code surfaces are not runtime-enforced by this adapter.
The master source and current planning state still describe Phase 1 as hook-free until the I-004 owner incorporates this completed amendment while editing those shared files.
